summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.2% YoY to INR15,448 million; VAR up 18.4% to INR13,816 million, EBITDA margin 17.9% of VAR.
summary.overview: Tenneco Clean Air India reported Q1 FY27 value added revenue (VAR) of INR13,816 million, up 18.4% YoY, with ART growing 27.9% and Clean Air and Powertrain growing 9.6%. EBITDA rose 7.9% YoY to INR2,469 million, with margin at 17.9% of VAR, down about 170 bps YoY and 43 bps QoQ as commodity inflation, rupee depreciation, Middle East-related costs and listed-company costs weighed. PAT was INR1,652 million, with management stating PAT growth tracked EBITDA growth once the prior-year Motocare one-time gain is excluded. Management said it had partially recovered non-indexed commodity costs from customers, with recovery still under discussion for the remainder.

financial_highlights.change: +7.9% YoY; margin down ~170 bps YoY and 43 bps QoQ (per analyst)
Prior-year quarter included one-time Motocare sale gain and other one-off income; PAT growth stated as similar to EBITDA growth excluding this

financial_highlights.metric: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions VAR

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: VAR of INR6,626 million, up 9.6% YoY. Management attributes gap versus ~mid-to-high-teens industry growth to EV exclusion, a leading Japanese PV OEM where Tenneco has no business, and GST-driven demand concentrated at that OEM.

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (suspension)
segments.commentary: VAR of INR7,190 million, up 27.9% YoY, now the larger segment by VAR. Capacity utilisation above 90%; new western India plant planned at about INR70 crore.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle Clean Air Solutions
segments.commentary: Value market share rose from 57% to 58% in FY2026 per management.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle shock absorbers and struts
segments.commentary: Value market share rose from 52% to 55% in FY2026 per management.

segments.name: Off-highway Clean Air Solutions
segments.commentary: Market share of 68% stated; later referred to as 60%+ in answers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex indicated at INR350-450 crore, funded through internal accruals; includes about INR140 crore for two already-announced plants and export-oriented investment; management said it may pull in or pull out based on demand and figures are indicative, not precise guidance.
Management expects demand to remain good through Q2 FY27 for Indian OEMs; margins expected to follow prior-year seasonal pattern.

Order book to be reported half-yearly; H1 order book, including domestic and export split, to be disclosed with Q2 results. Management said order book growth is unchanged from the earlier mid-teens outlook but gave no number.
Expects many new product launches from early calendar 2027 through 2029, including DaVinci semi-active and Clean Air wins.
Royalty stays at 2.5% of revenue net of intercompany sales.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex target INR350-450 crore (indicative), supporting double-digit top-line growth; split across Clean Air and Powertrain and ART.
Clean Air and Powertrain capacity utilisation upward of 80%; ART utilisation above 90%.
New ART plant in western India, investment about INR70 crore, already announced; total two announced plants about INR140 crore.
Capex-to-date for Q1 FY27 not disclosed; to be given with H1 results in September.
demand_pricing: Export order book split about 70:30 between Tenneco group entities and third-party OEMs; export order book historically 14-20% of total order book.

Management reported wins: ATV maiden order from a European OEM; heat shield order from Tenneco America; spark plug order from a large PV OEM (value not disclosed); PV exhaust program; CNG cold-end assembly; CV aftertreatment program; four new customers across DCx and conventional lines.
Management said the DaVinci suspension wins are rapid and cost delta vs conventional is only a few percentage points; no price deltas disclosed.

Commodity cost pressure: steel is indexed and back-to-back with OEMs; rubber, plastics, crude, LPG, CNG, argon not indexed and only partly recovered. Tariffs under Section 232 affect exhaust-part exports to the US.
Regulatory: BS-VII expected to add roughly 1.3x-1.5x content per vehicle, CAFE 3 about 1.2x-1.5x, per management, not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment drove the YoY EBITDA margin decline, and how much is cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose BU-level margins. YoY decline attributed to listed-company costs and Middle East-driven commodity inflation on non-indexed inputs; steel is back-to-back indexed with a quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Order book growth versus the earlier mid-teens target?
qa_highlights.answer: No number given. Management said the outlook is unchanged; order book will be reported half-yearly, with H1 at Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Clean Air growing ~10% versus an industry growing mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Served market excludes EV and a leading Japanese PV OEM where Tenneco has no business; management estimated apples-to-apples served market growth at 8-10%, against 9.6% achieved. Entry into that OEM expected via CAFE 3 around 2028-29.

qa_highlights.question: Did Hyundai supply disruption affect Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No impact, as Tenneco has limited position with that PV company.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and split by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: INR350-450 crore, indicative, across Clean Air/Powertrain and ART including two announced plants (~INR140 crore). Capex-to-date for Q1 not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of BS-VII and CAFE 3 on content per vehicle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly 1.3-1.5x content uplift from the combination, far below the BS-IV to BS-VI jump, with BS-VII specification still uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Export margins versus domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export margins are in line with or better than domestic margins; no separate figures.

risks_watch: Non-indexed commodity cost recovery (rubber, plastics, energy, argon) remains incomplete; EBITDA margin down ~170 bps YoY.
Middle East conflict duration and its effect on input costs and demand; management flagged potential Q3 impact if it deteriorates.
Export headwinds from Section 232 tariffs and weak Europe/Americas macro.
BS-VII specification and timing unclear; CAFE 3 entry at a large PV OEM expected 2028-29.
Order book, export split and H1 capex to be disclosed with Q2 results.
Management flagged possible pull-in or pull-out of capex based on demand.
key_quotes: But if you exclude Motocare, our PAT growth is similar to EBITDA growth. I want to be very clear on that.
So, I cannot give you a number. You know, order book we decided that because, you know, the thing with order book is that there's no steady order book , right?
So, for now -- at least, for now, I'd say assume that it's a 70-30 split between internal versus third-party OEMs, but that ratio can easily change.

But that year-over-year delta that you see, mainly comes to these two. It's moving from a private to a public company. And secondly, the commodity escalation that happened in the last quarter because of the Middle East war.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, the DaVinci suspension pipeline and export strategy, but cautious and evasive on order book value, BU-level margins, price deltas, capex-to-date and the BS-VII specification. They tied the YoY margin decline to listed-company costs and Middle East-driven non-indexed commodity inflation, with recovery still partial.
